sense: of a number: not divisible by two

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, one ending; ablative singular imparī
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.32 (Lewis & Short): stēllārum numerus pār an impar sit, nescītur
Verg. E. 8.75 (Lewis & Short): numerō deus impare gaudet
terms.comment: The opposite of pār, even: numerus pār, numerus impar. It also means unequal, no match for: impar esse + dative, “be unable to cope with” (Traupman 150; Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: stēllārum numerus pār an impar sit, nescītur
phrases.english: nobody knows whether the number of the stars is even or odd

sources: Lewis & Short: impar · Lewis & Short: par
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 150, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
